source_hypotheses: Reference Man: 20-30 y, 70 kg, 170 cm, Caucasian, Western European or North American habitat, climate 10-20 C (p.4, READ in the prior re-audit); a separate reference female of 58 kg (p.13); characteristics 'chosen within those limits with some degree of arbitrariness' (p.4).

'All values have been rounded to two significant figures' with four named exceptions (specific gravity; GI-tract, body-fat and CNS contents) and 'Many apparent discrepancies throughout this chapter are due to rounding' (pp.273-274). Table 110 sums to 70,102.4 g against 70,000.

Table 110 'includes only those elements for which the concentration was known in at least 50 % of the total body, including the skeleton' (p.327); 'when a value for the concentration of an element in skeleton was not known, no value for total body has been included' (p.286).
Total-body content is the SUM over organs and tissues; unknown tissues are assigned the known-tissue average (p.286); C, H, O, N computed from water/fat/protein/carbohydrate via Table 106 (p.287).

Common trace elements rest on 150 adult accidental-death victims from the United States (Tennessee / Oak Ridge); medians represent Reference Man; '<' means below detection in more than half the specimens (pp.274, 286) -- so B, Sn, Au, Mo, Cr are upper limits, not measurements.

Cs from Yamagata's Japanese subjects, transferred because no Western values existed (p.288); Co values 'arbitrarily based' on Tipton and Parr (p.288); Si is from Chapter 3, not a tissue sum (Table 110 note a).

Na, K, Cl, I can be estimated otherwise: Na 70-93 g from isotope dilution / activation against 100 g by chemistry; K 133-145 g; I 13 g is a thyroid + extrathyroidal estimate that 'may exceed' 13 mg (pp.287-288).

grade_evidence: (1) ICRP 23 Chapter 2, Table 110 (pp.327-328), READ: every value that decides a binder the owner prints is ICRP's to the gram -- P 780, N 1800 (and O C H Ca K S Na Cl Mg) -- and body mass 70,000 g. On ICRP's own values and denominator the CI binder is P at 10.714 with N second, the photosphere binder P at 1913.2; ICRP's two-significant-figure rounding cannot reach any flip threshold (P would need < 715.7 g or < 588.7 g; N > 2385 g). The ICRP leg, as far as it decides the binder, STANDS. (2) The '(ICRP)' attribution is NARROWED at source: 21 of 59 owner values are Table 110's, 14 differ (five of them against printed upper limits), 24 are not in the table -- among them Li, the only element within 9 % of flipping the photosphere binder. The 9 % near miss is an Emsley datum, not an ICRP one; on ICRP alone the runner-up is K, 2.93x behind. (3) The composite grade does not rest on the ICRP leg alone: the prior re-audit's moved or contested data -- CI N (LBP25 1965 ppm, READ there) flipping CI to N; photospheric Li (AAG21 0.96, carried) and payload Li (7 vs 2.17 mg, carried tertiary) deciding P vs Li at the photosphere -- are untouched by this read. So DATA-DEPENDENT stands, now with its ICRP component closed: the data dependence is in the destination columns and in a non-ICRP payload element, not in ICRP 23. Not WRONG: no computed contradiction of any measurement as defined; the owner's 14 non-matching values are attribution discrepancies.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS for the binder labels: settled photospheric Li with eps_Li - eps_P >= -4.397 at payload Li 7 mg (or a primary whole-body Li for the 70 kg male below 7.63 mg -- ICRP 23 Table 110 prints none; Table 108's tail is OPEN in this OCR), and settled CI N >= ~2280 ppm at P 989; or the tree printing 'P or Li / P or N within the data's spread'. A legible scan of Table 108 (pp.289-324) would settle whether ICRP 23 gives Li at all and would read the Cl percent cell. To WRONG: a computed contradiction of a measurement as defined; none approached.
